transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, uh, mostly because of my work physical. The doctor there said my weight was too low and that I should come in, so… here I am. I don’t know, I don’t really feel bad about it. Honestly I feel kind of lighter on my feet when I play basketball, and at the garage it’s nice not feeling so weighed down crawling around cars all day. My buddy at work always jokes the younger guys move quicker, so I guess I took that to heart a little.
Have you been intentionally trying to lose weight or avoid gaining weight, even if it means eating less than you might want?

I mean… yeah, I guess I do watch it pretty close. Like if the scale bumps up even a pound, or my jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I’m getting soft, you know? And then I’m thinking I’ll be slower getting around under cars at work, or running up and down the court.

It’s probably stupid, but it gets in my head. I’ll eat less if I think that’s happening. My jeans used to fit different when I was younger—well, everybody’s did, I guess—but now I notice every little change.
Do you ever make yourself sick or use laxatives, diet pills, or anything like that to control your weight?

Uh… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not doing anything like that. I’ve heard guys at the gym talk about supplements and all that stuff, but I don’t really get into it—half of them are just trying to look good in tank tops, you know? I mostly just try to keep an eye on what I’m eating. Nothing like making myself sick or taking pills or whatever.
Do you find yourself preoccupied with your body shape or weight most of the time, even when other people might not notice a change?

Yeah… I mean, maybe more than I should. It’s not like I’m staring in the mirror all day or anything, but if I see the scale go up even a pound, or my jeans feel a little tighter, it kind of sticks in my head.

Then I start thinking I’m getting soft, and if I get soft I’ll be slower at work, crawling around cars, or slower on the court. Which sounds ridiculous saying it out loud, because nobody else is probably noticing. My wife probably wouldn’t even—well, I don’t know. But yeah, I notice it, and then I think about it for a while.
Do you judge yourself mainly based on your body weight or shape, like feeling that your value as a person depends on it?

I don’t know if I’d say my value as a person, exactly. That sounds… big. I mean, I know being a good husband, showing up to work, doing the job right—those things matter too.

But then again, if I feel like I’m getting out of shape, it does mess with how I see myself. Like I feel lazy or like I’m slipping. My dad used to say you can tell a lot about a guy by how he takes care of his truck, which is funny because half the cars I work on are disasters inside, fast food bags everywhere… but anyway.

I guess I don’t really know where the line is. I don’t think I’m worthless because of my weight, but it definitely affects my head more than I’d like.
Has this concern about your weight or shape ever caused you significant distress or gotten in the way of your daily life, like affecting your relationships, work, or other activities?

I mean… I’m still doing my stuff. I go to work at the garage, I’m not missing shifts or anything, and I still play in my basketball league. Though last week one of the guys was joking about how I run around like I’m still twenty-five, which, you know, I definitely feel it the next morning.

But at home, yeah… it’s caused some friction. I don’t really like sitting down for regular family meals lately, and my wife notices. Then people start asking if I’m okay, or why I’m not eating with everybody, and I get kind of irritated because I don’t want it to be a whole thing. So… it hasn’t stopped my life, exactly, but it’s definitely making home more tense than it should be.
Do you ever feel like you’re overweight or out of shape even when other people, or maybe the mirror, don’t really show that you are?

Yeah, I guess I do. Not like I look in the mirror and think I’m huge or anything, but if the scale bumps up even one pound, or my jeans feel tighter, my head goes right to, “Great, I’m getting soft.”

And then I start thinking I’ll be slower moving around cars at work, or not as quick up and down the court. Which is probably kind of dumb, because one pound isn’t going to change how I move, but it feels like it means something, you know? Like I’m slipping.
Do you ever skip meals, follow a strict diet, or exercise a lot more than usual to try to control your weight?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t call it some official diet or anything. It’s more like I’ve got my own little rules, I guess.

Most mornings I just have coffee and get moving. Then later, if things slow down at the shop, I might have a small sandwich, or maybe half of whatever’s around. The shop’s always running late, somebody needs a part, somebody’s car is making a noise they can’t describe—so it’s easy to just keep it simple.

And at home it’s busy too, so I kind of feel better sticking to my own routine instead of sitting down to a big meal. It feels more controlled that way, I guess.
Can you tell me about your current weight and whether it’s changed recently, and if so, how much weight you may have lost and over what period of time?

Well, the work physical is kind of what kicked all this off. I had to get checked out for work, and the doctor there said my weight was too low. I don’t know… I guess I didn’t see it that way.

To me I just feel lighter, like I move better. Playing basketball, I feel quicker up and down the court, and at the garage I don’t feel as weighed down crawling around or being on my feet all day. So when they made it sound like a problem, I was kind of surprised.
Can you tell me what you currently weigh, and whether that’s changed over the past few months?

I don’t know the exact number off the top of my head… the work physical is what made it a thing, really. The doctor there said I was too low, and I kind of remember thinking, “Low compared to what?” because I’m still doing my job, you know?

Like at the garage, being under cars and on my feet all day, I feel lighter, not dragged down. Same with basketball — I feel quicker getting up and down the court. So yeah, I guess it has gone down some over the past few months, but I didn’t really see it as a problem until that physical.
Can you estimate how much weight you’ve lost over the past few months, even roughly?

I mean… I don’t have a clean number for you. That’s part of why this feels strange, because I wasn’t really tracking it like that.

The work physical is what got me sitting here, honestly. The doctor there said my weight was too low, and I guess I heard it, but in my head I’m thinking, well, I’m still moving around fine. At basketball I feel lighter on my feet, and at the garage I don’t feel as weighed down when I’m up and down all day.

So… roughly, yeah, it’s gone down, but I don’t know how much to say exactly.
Would you say the weight loss was something you were intentionally trying to achieve, even if it meant staying below what might be a normal weight for your height and build?

I don’t know if I’d say I was trying to be, like, under some number. I don’t really think of it that way.

I guess I do have my own way of doing things now, though. Most mornings it’s just coffee, then later maybe a small sandwich or half of whatever’s around. The shop runs late a lot, and then the house is busy when I get home, and honestly it just feels easier sticking to that. Like if I keep it simple, I feel better, less… I don’t know, thrown off.

So yeah, I guess I’m choosing it in that sense, but I wasn’t sitting there thinking about a “normal weight” chart or anything.
Can you tell me approximately what your current weight is, and how that compares to what you think is a normal or healthy weight for your height and build?

I’m not sure of the exact number right now. The work physical is what kind of kicked all this off — the doctor there said my weight was too low for me, I guess for my height and build.

But it’s hard for me to see it that way, because at basketball I just feel lighter on my feet, like I can move better. And at the garage, you know, I’m crawling around, standing, bending all day, and I don’t feel as weighed down. So compared to what they’re calling normal or healthy, yeah, I guess I’m under that… I just don’t always feel like it’s a bad thing.
Even though you said you weren’t focused on a specific number, do you think you’re currently under what most people would consider a normal or healthy weight for someone your height?

Yeah… I mean, I guess if you put it that way, probably. The doctor at the work physical said my weight was too low, and that’s really what got me here.

It’s just hard for me to think of it like “unhealthy,” because when I’m playing basketball I feel quicker, lighter on my feet. And at the garage, being up and down all day, leaning over cars and moving around, I don’t feel as weighed down. So… yeah, most people might say I’m under where I should be, but I don’t really feel it the same way.
Can you tell me what your height is and whether the doctor at your work physical mentioned how your current weight compares to the minimum normal weight for someone your height?

I’m not great with the exact numbers off the top of my head. I mean, I know my height, but I don’t really keep track of it like that, and the work physical is what sort of got this whole thing started.

The doctor there said my weight was too low for me, like for my height, yeah. I don’t remember him saying it like “minimum normal weight” exactly, or maybe he did and I just kind of tuned out after “too low.” I was thinking about getting back to the garage because we were slammed that week.

But yeah, he was basically saying I was under where I should be. I just… I don’t feel it the same way, you know? Playing basketball, I feel lighter on my feet, and at work I don’t feel as weighed down moving around cars all day.
Can you tell me your exact height and what your current weight is, so I can better understand how it compares?

I don’t know the exact weight right now… I know that’s what you’re asking, but I haven’t really been keeping a number in my head.

The work physical is what got me here, really. That doctor said my weight was too low for me, like for my height. I kind of heard that and then my mind went to work stuff — we had a bunch of cars backed up at the garage, and I was thinking about getting back there.

But yeah, he said it was low. I just have a hard time feeling worried about it, because on the basketball court I feel lighter, like I can move better, and at work I don’t feel as weighed down crawling around and bending over cars all day.
Can you please tell me your exact height and your most recent weight measurement from your work physical?

I know, you’re asking for the exact numbers… I don’t really have them in my head. The work physical is what got me here, though—the doctor said my weight was too low for my height.

I guess I didn’t hang onto the actual number because I was more thinking about getting back to the garage, and then later I was thinking how I don’t feel bad exactly. Like, when I’m playing basketball I feel lighter on my feet, and at work I don’t feel as weighed down moving around cars all day. But yeah, he said it was too low.
Can you please give me your exact height in feet and inches, and your most recent weight in pounds from the work physical?

I’m sorry, I really don’t have the exact feet-and-inches and pounds number in my head from that physical. I know that’s what you need.

What I remember is the doctor there saying my weight was too low for my height, and that’s what pushed all this along. I guess I didn’t lock onto the number because I was thinking about getting back to the garage, and honestly part of me was thinking, well, I feel lighter on my feet playing basketball and not as weighed down at work, so it didn’t hit me the way he probably meant it to.
Can you please tell me your height in feet and inches and the exact weight in pounds that the doctor recorded during your work physical?

I really don’t have the exact number, doctor. I know I keep circling around it, but the work physical is what got me sent here—the doctor there said my weight was too low for my height.

I guess I didn’t hang on to the pounds or the feet-and-inches part because I was thinking about getting back to the garage. And honestly, I don’t feel that bad about it. On the basketball court I feel lighter on my feet, and at work I don’t feel as weighed down crawling around cars all day. So I know he said it was too low, but the exact weight… I don’t know it.

Can you ask someone close to you, like your wife, to provide your exact height and the weight number the doctor recorded during your work physical? I really need that information to help me understand what’s going on.

Yeah, I mean… I can ask my wife, sure. She’s probably better with that stuff than I am—she keeps papers and remembers numbers. I just kind of, you know, heard “too low for your height” at the work physical and then my mind went to getting back to the garage.

The doctor there said my weight was too low, that’s what started all this. But to me, it hasn’t felt like some big emergency. I feel lighter when I’m playing basketball, and at work I don’t feel as weighed down moving around the shop. But yeah… I can ask her if she has the exact height and weight number.
